extracted.intended_audience: healthcare organizations, in-house and agency PR professionals, communications teams
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for planning and executing public relations campaigns for healthcare providers, hospitals, and health organizations, including press releases, media pitching, patient stories, and compliance checks. Emphasizes audience understanding, measurable tactics, and legal/regulatory safeguards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand your audience and medium
rubrics_metrics.description: The better you understand the people you’re speaking to, the better you’ll predict their emotional responses to what you’re putting out and the sharper your decisions will be throughout your healthcare public relations campaign.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Segment audiences, select channels that reach those segments, anticipate emotional reactions, and tailor message tone and detail to the audience and medium (e.g., social, broadcast, print). "Understand your audience and medium" is listed as a core best practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage press decision-makers
rubrics_metrics.description: If you’re trying to get a healthcare story featured in traditional media such as newspapers or broadcast, propose the story to reporters and producers — these are the people who will actually grant life to the content you want publicized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pitch as close as possible to the ultimate source; research reporters’ previous articles and preferred audiences; weave that reconnaissance into your proposal to increase pickup likelihood.

rubrics_metrics.name: Localize your story
rubrics_metrics.description: People respond more strongly to news that concerns them, their families and their communities than to news from far afield.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight aspects of PR pieces that hit close to home for the target audience (geographic or community relevance). Use proximity to transform an abstract story into an emotional, attention-grabbing one.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proofread before publishing (accuracy is key)
rubrics_metrics.description: Especially when it comes to medical information, accuracy is key. The last thing you want when health is at stake is to mislead people, overstate a point or misinterpret a piece of scientific evidence in the public eye.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a proofreading step for every item; verify scientific claims and data; prevent misstatements that could trigger a communications crisis or harm public trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check for HIPAA and FDA compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Beware of HIPAA and FDA rules — HIPAA Privacy Rule sets out safeguards against unauthorized disclosure that you will need to comply with in your medical PR pieces. Material defined as “marketing” under HIPAA criteria will require more steps in advance of publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm patient privacy protections before publishing stories; determine whether content qualifies as marketing and follow required notice/authorization pathways; ensure any product or therapeutic claims comply with FDA requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use clear, straightforward language to build trust
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective medical PR prioritizes clear, straightforward language that meets audiences where they are. By breaking down complicated concepts into their most essential points, a well-crafted communications campaign empowers patients to feel informed, included and respected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid jargon; translate complexity into clarity; prioritize readability and empathetic tone to reduce patient uncertainty and distrust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spotlight clinical outcomes, innovations, patient stories, and third-party validation
rubrics_metrics.description: An experienced PR partner can help hospitals and healthcare organizations build trust and strengthen community goodwill by spotlighting clinical outcomes, innovative contributions, patient stories and credible third-party validation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use multiple proof points (data, patient narratives, external endorsements) together to reinforce expertise and compassion; ensure ethical sourcing and consent for patient stories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat education as an inherent goal of healthcare PR
rubrics_metrics.description: Healthcare PR often centers on medical advancements, emerging health challenges, treatment options and preventative care—information that can directly impact people’s lives. Education is not an add-on to healthcare PR; it is inherent to it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design communications to inform and empower communities (clarify complex topics, explain implications), not solely to promote the organization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create community through shared narratives and resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Public relations in healthcare can bring people together by showing them that their lives are part of a larger tapestry. Publishing articles or collecting diverse patient experiences cultivates a sense of hope and togetherness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use patient stories and condition-focused content to foster connection; curate content formats (blogs, series) that enable ongoing community engagement while protecting privacy and consent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grow thought leadership via strategic exposure
rubrics_metrics.description: Public relations helps organizations earn recognition for innovations and positions them as thought leaders through strategic media coverage, speaking engagements and savvy publishing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pursue earned media, targeted speaking opportunities, and high-value publishing to solidify leadership; align spokespersons, topics, and evidence to the organization’s expertise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leverage data-driven strategies and audience segmentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Data has enormous potential to help you find, message and resonate with your target audience to achieve results (e.g., Spring Health’s data-driven strategy produced increases in qualified leads and hires).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use analytics to identify high-value segments; tailor messaging and channel mix based on data; iterate campaigns according to performance metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Map engagement journeys and conduct stakeholder interviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Clear audience segments and mapped engagement journeys, plus stakeholder interviews, guide strategy by revealing processes, needs and opportunities for improvement (as used in the EXPAREL campaign).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document user/provider journeys, interview internal and external stakeholders to surface barriers and opportunities, and align touchpoints to desired outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure campaign performance with concrete metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Successful campaigns report measurable outcomes (examples: 113% increase in provider-qualified leads; 307% more providers connected; increases in traffic and organic sessions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define KPIs (leads, hires, direct traffic, organic sessions, conversions), track results, and use them to demonstrate ROI and refine strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use benefit-driven creative to educate and resonate
rubrics_metrics.description: Benefit-driven ad creative is an effective tool to educate and resonate with patients and providers (EXPAR EL key takeaway).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Craft creative that emphasizes concrete benefits to target audiences, pairing educational content with persuasive value propositions to drive engagement and conversion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collect and publish patient stories ethically
rubrics_metrics.description: Personal narratives are incredibly powerful — real, raw stories tap into emotional responses and elicit hope, raise awareness, and garner positive impact (e.g., New York–Presbyterian’s "Patient Stories" series).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain informed consent, anonymize when necessary, respect HIPAA and privacy rules, and ensure stories are used respectfully without sensationalizing patients’ experiences.
